E1 Repeated-item recognition Entity memory 1 2 4 Instruction. Hard: Observe and remember each batch of items. After the first batch, place the one item that appeared in any of the previous five batches into the submission tray. Success. Every repeated item stably deposited in its submission tray (first batch is observation-only). / / H. 3/5/7 batches, 4/4/6 objects per batch and 2/4/6 submissions. Repeats come from the previous 1, up to 3, or up to 5 batches. E2 Object-coded keypad arithmetic Entity memory 1 3 4 Instruction. Observe the visible entity-value associations, remember them, decode the physical expression, and enter its exact result using only the closed gripper fingertips on the nine keys. Success. All digits of the exact result entered in order after effective press-release, with no wrong, missing or extra press. / / H. 3/4/6 object-value bindings shown, then hidden; the board then shows an arithmetic expression over the same objects (Medium and Hard repeat objects), whose result is typed on keys 19. F1 Unknown button mapping Feedback-rule learning 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Probe the four unmarked buttons and remember how each moves the slider. After the slider resets and the goal appears, reach the visible goal on the 4 by 4 grid using the fewest presses. Success. Slider reaches the visible goal after the slider reset. held button does not retrigger, and out-of-bounds input has no effect. / / H. linear track, 3 by 3 grid, or 4 by 4 grid, with 2/4/4 buttons. Shortest routes are 13/23/46 steps. Exploration cost is recorded separately. F2 Color-block arrangement by feedback Feedback-rule learning 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Place one colored block in each slot, then press and release the confirmation button on the right. The brief feedback gives the number of correct positions. Infer the hidden permutation in as few attempts as possible. Success. Correct arrangement found within the submission budget: one released, supported block per slot, stable 0.5 s, then button released (press on an incomplete layout is not submission). / / H. 3/4/5 blocks and slots; 5/6/7 valid submissions. Research preprint 52 mmlab@SIGS P1 Incremental meal orders Process memory 1 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Remember the initial orders and two additional orders shown later. Place all requested ingredients into the indicated containers; each additional order adds to earlier demand. Success. Each container holds exactly the requested types and quantities. / / H. 2/2/3 containers and 4/5/7 deposits. All levels start with two orders requesting four items. Later additions are none, one order adding one item, or two orders adding two and one items. P2 Steamer-stack order restoration Process memory 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Remove the lid, remember the dim sum order as you unstack the baskets from top to bottom onto the mats, then restack them in the same order from bottom to top on the left steamer pot and replace the lid without using any distractor baskets. Success. Correct original baskets restacked in original order on the left pot, stable, lid placed; the final stack holds no extra basket (setting one aside temporarily is allowed). / / H. 3/4/4 layers to restore; 0/0/2 distractor baskets that look the same outside but hold different dumplings. S1 Tray-layout restoration Spatial memory 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Remember the four colored slots, observe the carousel rotation, then place each colored block into its original matching slot after the carousel stops. Success. All four blocks in their original tray-relative cells. / / H. 12 slow rotation segments in one direction, 34 segments with reversals, or 56 faster segments with repeated reversals. All levels use four colors, four placements and the same placement tolerances. S2 Hidden-hazard navigation Spatial memory 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Remember the briefly lit forbidden cells. Press and release the arrow buttons to move one cell per press. Reach the ring without entering forbidden cell or leaving the board. Do not touch the slider. Success. Slider supported and inside the board throughout, never touching hazard, fully in the goal and stable 0.5 (any hazard contact or leaving the board precludes success). / / H. 4 4/5 5/6 6 boards with 3/7/12 hazard cells; shortest routes of 6/10/14 steps in the first instance. M1 Workpiece tracking and route replay Integrated memory 1 2 3 Instruction. Remember the target location and station route. Track the target through the cover exchanges, uncover it, and move it through the required stations in order. Success. Target retrieved and initial station plus visits replayed in order, each placement released and stable (temporary tabletop placements do not count). / / H. 4/4/6 stations and 3/5/7 exchanges, including 0/1/2 exchanges unrelated to the target. Replay requires 4/5/6 placements. Medium and Hard include at least one and two revisits, respectively. Research preprint 53 mmlab@SIGS M2 Card-matching game Integrated memory 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Press and release cards yellow button to turn it face up, revealing at most two unmatched cards at time. Matching pictures stay face up; mismatches turn face down automatically. Wait until the flip or pair result finishes before selecting another card. Remember the pictures and their positions and match every pair. Success. All pairs matched and held face-up (mismatches are exploration, not failure). / / H. 2 2/2 4/4 4 layouts with 2/4/8 pairs. Act tasks Ten tasks that test timing and precision, with the operation stated in the instruction. DR1 Conveyor pickup 1 2 DR2 Light-cued response 2 3 3 DR3 Timed passage through cyclic gates 1 3 4 4 4 Dynamic response Instruction. Hard: Pick up all 7 packages on the conveyor belt and place them in the central collection tray. Success. All required packages stably deposited within budget, none missed (a package that leaves the reach region counts as missed). / / H. 3/5/7 packages arrive on the conveyor, and all of them must be collected into the central tray. Dynamic response Instruction. Hard: Press the currently illuminated button within 2.6 seconds and release within 1 second. Respond correctly to all 10 cues; never press an unlit button. Success. Ten correct press-release events, each released within 1 s. repeated cue needs separate event. / / H. Cue-to-press deadlines are 4.0/3.2/2.6 s. Button geometry, ten-cue count and release timing stay fixed. Dynamic response Instruction. Hard: Grasp the eraser, time the moving gates, and pass through the blue then the orange opening to place the eraser stably in the green tray behind them. Withdraw the whole gripper past the outer gate before they close. Do not touch any gate, frame or rail. Success. The eraser is carried through each open gate in order and left supported in the tray. Dropping or throwing it into the tray earns only the gate-passage credit. When gate first closes after the eraser has passed, both arms must be clear of its passage on the near side (arm contact with gate, frame or rail during that closure precludes success). / / H. One gate fully open for 6.6/6.0 per 11.2/10.6 cycle on Easy/Medium; on Hard, two gates with 18.4 and 9.2 cycles whose shared openings alternate between 3.6 s, too short for the measured 5.1 action chain, and 6.4 s. DR4 Tray carrying with loose balls Dynamic response (stability) 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Carry the tray of four balls by its handle from START to DESTINATION around the two staggered columns, keeping each ball inside its marked circle. Set the tray down stably, release it and retreat. Do not touch the balls or hit anything. Success. All balls stay on the tray and inside their circles throughout; tray delivered within 20 mm, vertical error <3 mm, released, stable for the last 2 (a ball leaving its circle, with 0.5 mm tolerance, is latched failure). / / H. 2/3/4 balls, 0/1/2 pillars, and allowed drift radii of 30/25/20 mm. Research preprint 54 mmlab@SIGS PR1 Resistance adjustment Precise execution 1 3 4 PR2 Voltage setting 1 2 PR3 Pen tracing 1 2 3 3 4 Instruction. Adjust the resistance between the left terminal and wiper to 𝑅 Ω, then release the slider and keep that reading for 0.5 seconds. (𝑅 per episode.) Success. Reading within 0.2/0.15/0.12 Ω, held for 0.5 after release. / / H. One target per episode on numbered major tick, an unnumbered minor tick, or between minor ticks: 7/21/21 distinct targets, e.g. 10/16/35.75 Ω. Precise execution Instruction. Adjust the output voltage to 𝑉 V, then release the knob and keep that reading for 1 second. (𝑉 per episode.) Success. Reading within 1/0.5/0.5 for 1 after release. / / H. One target per episode on numbered major tick, an unnumbered minor tick, or between minor ticks: 12/33/33 distinct targets, e.g. 160/165/147 V. Precise execution Instruction. Grasp the marker and trace the complete visible path, then lift. Success. At least 98% of the reference path lies within 3 mm of ink and the RMS distance from the ink to the path is at most 2 mm. Only ink from actual contact counts. / / H. straight line, an curve with two half-waves, or curve with four half-waves. All paths are 350 mm long with 3 mm centerline tolerance. Curved paths have minimum radii of about 54/25 mm. PR4 Cloth folding and flat placement Precise execution 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Fold the hexagonal cloth once into the displayed trapezoid, align its paired edges, release it fully and leave it stable. Success. Required fold made, layers and corners aligned within tolerance, inside the target frame, released and lying flat and stable. / / H. Midline fold into two-layer rectangle; diagonal fold into two-layer triangle; single fold of hexagon along its symmetry axis into two-layer trapezoid. All pieces have the same area (400 cm2), mass, and material. PR5 Oriented stamping Precise execution 1 2 3 Instruction. Pick up square stamp and stamp once, fully inside the blue box, with its arrow aligned to the target arrow. Do not drag or stamp twice. Return the stamp to its holder in its original orientation and release it. Success. Exactly one imprint with all four rotated corners inside the frame and arrow within tolerance, no smear; stamp returned, gripper withdrawn. The arrow defines the orientation over the full 360. / / H. Frames of 100/80/74 mm and orientation tolerances of 5/2/1; targets sampled from 8/32/320 directions; minimum centered margins of 14.6/4.6/1.6 mm. Research preprint 55 mmlab@SIGS PR6 Domino chain to bell Precise execution 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Stand the dominos anywhere inside the continuous curve band, in order along the curve. Push the first one so the chain of contacts rings the bell. Repair fallen or stalled segments using as few pushes as possible. Success. Dominoes released and held in the same valid order for 0.5 s, the first one pushed, and the chain falling along the band to strike the bell. / / H. 5/7/9 dominoes; heights of 10.24 (uniform)/8.3212.00/7.6813.44 cm; band spans of 41.3/57.3/76.1 cm. Mind2Act tasks Ten tasks that combine remembered state and physical outcomes in one loop. CP01 Conveyor meal assembly Cumulative progress 1 2 4 Instruction. At the start, watch the reference meal trays pass on the conveyor and remember the three food types on each. Then prepare the corresponding empty meal trays on the table and fill each with the same three food types from the continuously moving supply. Success. All requested foods stably in the correct meal trays; Medium and Hard also require the meal trays retrieved from the stack (no recirculation or replacement supply). / / H. 1/2/3 orders with 3/6/9 food items. Easy provides one meal tray. Medium and Hard require retrieving 2 and 3 meal trays from the left stack, respectively. Belt speed remains 0.025 m/s across all levels. CP02 Rotating-cake decoration Prerequisites and repair 1 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Remember each macaron and its place on the still cake shown for three seconds. Open the ingredient-box lid, press the green button and recreate the arrangement as the cake rotates. Then press the red button, wait for the cake to stop, and place the cake cover over it. Success. Full layout placed and all preparation and cleanup steps done; Hard also requires the turntable stopped and at rest before the cover is placed. / / H. 4/6/6 macarons at speeds of 12/20/28/s. Easy starts open and running. Medium and Hard add opening the box lid and pressing the green button. Hard also adds the stopping and covering sequence. CP03 Moving-rack loading Cumulative progress 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Load 7 upright plates into the moving empty slots without disturbing other plates. Tilt the lever fully toward the back of the machine, away from the robot, release it, then press the green button before loading. Success. Every plate supported by both side supports and the base, earlier plates undisturbed. / / H. 3/5/7 plates at 12/16/20 mm/s. All levels start with the green button; Medium first sets the lever upright in the middle, Hard tilts it fully back. Support gaps are approximately 36.5/30.5/26.5 mm. Hard reverses direction with 0.6 end transition while insertions occur at cruise speed. Research preprint mmlab@SIGS CP04 Temperature-controlled cooking Feedback-driven adjustment 1 2 4 Instruction. Hard: Open the drawer. Pour each required jar into the pot in the remembered recipe order, returning jars upright and caps to the tray, then cover the pot. Turn the black knob to HEAT and press the green button; within 2 after 80 C, switch to KEEP WARM, then press it again. Success. Ingredients added in remembered order before HEAT, KEEP WARM selected within the window before shutdown, and jars and caps returned; Medium and Hard also require the drawer opened and the pot covered. / / H. 2/2/3 ordered ingredients from four jars, and HEAT must be switched to KEEP WARM within 4/3/2 after the pot reaches 80 (green band up to 90/87.5/85 C). All levels return the jars upright and their caps to the tray; Medium and Hard add opening the drawer and covering the pot. Geometric tolerances remain unchanged. CP05 Piano replay Sequence and plan execution 1 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Set volume to MAX and release the slider. Pick up both side mallets, press the triangle-marked button and watch the demonstration while holding both, then reproduce the twelve key presses in order using either mallet. Return and release both mallets, release all keys, withdraw your arms, and keep volume at MAX. Success. Effective strikes in the remembered sequence (rhythm need not match), mallets returned and arms withdrawn; Hard also requires the volume kept at MAX. / / H. 7/14/21 candidate keys, 8/8/12 events and 1/2/2 mallets. Easy uses the central mallet; Medium and Hard pick up and return both side mallets together, and Hard also sets the volume slider from MIN to MAX and keeps it there. Either mallet may strike. CP06 Produce weighing on balance Feedback-driven adjustment 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: With the empty scale stable, press ZERO. Move all fruit and vegetables from the left tray onto the left scale pan. Balance the scale using the weights on the right and by physically moving the sliding weight, then release them and keep the pointer in the green zone. Success. All produce on the left pan, the weights needed for balance on the right pan, nothing dropped, and the pointer inside the green zone and stable for 1 s; Medium and Hard also require ZERO pressed on the empty scale, and Hard the sliding weight at its target position. / / H. 1/2/3 produce items; Medium and Hard first press ZERO on the empty scale; weight sets of 2 50+2 100 g/50400 g/50400 g, with 040 sliding weight added on Hard; green zones of 10/8/5 g; 9/16/80 candidate states, with unique solution on Hard. CP07 Bridge building for toy car Sequence and plan execution 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Build stable bridge across the gap with continuous wheel paths on both sides. Choose suitable pieces by shape and size from the stock, which includes extra blocks, and leave unused blocks aside. Release the bridge pieces, then press and release the button and let the car drive across to the opposite bank. Success. Piers, caps and deck stably in place, button triggered, car upright and across the finish (unused distractor stock allowed). / / H. River widths of 18/28/36 cm; 1 pier and 2 spans/2 piers and 3 spans/2 unequal piers, sloped spans, and U-shaped ramp supports; stock of 8/18/28 pieces, of which 8/13/13 are needed. Research preprint 57 mmlab@SIGS CP08 Block structure from shown blueprint Prerequisites and repair 1 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Remember the briefly shown front view, then build the structure from memory, centred in the marked area and aligned with the table reference line. If the base is misplaced, move the beam above it aside and rebuild; put the roof ridge-up on the cylinders. Use only reference-colour blocks and release everything. Success. Colors, shapes, positions, orientation and support match the blueprint; beam and roof each borne by two blocks; stable 1 (Hard 5 s) after release (holding the structure up does not count; 90 roof error rejected). / / H. 3 cuboids in 2 layers/3 cuboids and 1 cylinder in 3 layers/6 blocks in 4 layers with prism roof; 0/1/2 distractors; 6/4/4 mm tolerance; 1/1/5 hold after release. CP09 Whiteboard restoration Prerequisites and repair 2 3 4 Instruction. Hard: Remember the briefly shown original drawing on the whiteboard. Erase the added strokes, uncap the pens of the colors needed, and redraw any original strokes you erased, so the board matches the original. Success. Final board matches the original in color, shape and layout: extra strokes removed, over-erased parts redrawn; Medium/Hard include uncapping. / / H. 2/3/4 original elements in 1/2/3 colors; added strokes of one line/a long and short crossing line/two long lines and an extra circle. The board starts on raised stand; the reference procedure first lays it flat on the table, though only the final board is scored. CP10 Return or dodge incoming balls Predictive decision 1 2 3 4 Instruction. Predict each ball from the launchers settled aim. After two practice balls, use the sliding blocker to return every white ball to the far net and let every red ball pass untouched into the near net. Wait for each ball to settle before the next shot. Success. Every scored ball correct: white returned to the far net, red cleared into the near net (two practice balls unscored). / / H. 5/8/12 scored balls, of which 2/4/6 are red; shots (direct/single-bounce/double-bounce) of 3/2/0 on Easy, 2/4/2 on Medium and 2/5/5 on Hard; countdowns of 4/3/2 s.
